title: Filtered continuity of internal derived invariants for a profinite group
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group. Write $\mathcal A_J(R)$ for internal $R$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an $R$-linear action of $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], and $\Gamma_{R,J}$ for the submodule fixed after every profinite base change. Use its ordinary total right derived functor [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], and put $R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N)=H^q(R\Gamma_{R,J}(N[0]))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every small filtered category $I$ (nonempty, with a common target for every finite diagram) and diagram $(N_i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathcal A_J(R)$, forgetting the action creates its filtered colimit: its underlying module is the sheaf colimit, with the induced action. For every $q\geq0$ the canonical map
$$\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N_i)\longrightarrow R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(\operatorname{colim}_{i\in I}N_i)$$
is an isomorphism of internal $R$-modules. The legs are exactly the maps induced by the original colimit coprojections. All indexing categories, profinite parameters and sheaves lie in the chosen compatible universes. No discreteness, finite generation, norm completeness, or bounded cohomological dimension is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0739, lemma-colim-works-over-collection, with the coherent profinite action-topos presentation. Agent-formulated internal derived-invariant specialization; the proof must verify coherent objects and the relative comparison, not merely cite AB5.

proof.text: First construct the colimit without using invariants. On the finite-cover profinite site, [lem-weil-pbc-site-filtered-colimit-sections-finite-coverings] computes filtered abelian sheaf colimits on sections; [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] gives the same colimit with its $R$-module structure. Thus put $N(S)=\operatorname{colim}_i N_i(S)$. For $g\in C(S,J)$ define $g[m_i]=[gm_i]$. Equivariance of the transition maps makes this well-defined; the action laws, linearity and restriction compatibility follow by applying each equation to a representative. This is an internal action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Its coprojections are equivariant. For an equivariant cocone, the unique underlying module map sends $[m_i]$ to its given image; this formula commutes with $g$ and all restrictions, so is equivariant. Consequently forgetting the action creates this filtered colimit, with the original coprojections.

source.place: Tag 0738 (sites.tex, lemma-directed-colimits-sections) and Tag 03CO (sites-modules.tex, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves); induced action checked directly

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-action-coherent-presentation] to $J$. Use its site $P_J$, ring $\mathcal R_J$ and exact additive equivalence $\Phi$. Put $F_i=\Phi(N_i)$ and $F=\Phi(N)$. An equivalence transports the colimit universal property: maps out of $\Phi(N)$ correspond, under its inverse, to maps out of $N$, so the transported coprojections make $F$ the module-sheaf colimit of the $F_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], $F_{ab}=\operatorname{colim}_i(F_i)_{ab}$ in abelian sheaves on $P_J$. All objects and arrows are small by the presentation's universe convention. The objects $tS$ are representables in this finite-limit site, hence coherent by that lemma; all iterated fibre products of finite-cover members are still objects of the same site. This verifies the compactness and intersection requirements of the cohomology-continuity route, including for non-discrete $J$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coherent profinite action-space realization of the filtered-passage input

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites] to the constant diagram of sites $P_J$ indexed by $I^{\mathrm{op}}$, all transition and cocone functors being identities. This meets [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-of-sites]: $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is cofiltered, all covers are finite, identity functors preserve covers and covering pullbacks, and the category colimit is $P_J$ (each object and arrow in a constant diagram has exactly its original representative). Use coefficients $(F_i)_{ab}$ and their original transition maps. Fix $i_0\in I$ and any $T\in P_J$. The cited theorem gives the comparison over $(i_0\downarrow I)$. Its colimit is the colimit over $I$, with the same coprojections: a cocone on the forward-arrow category extends at $j$ by choosing arrows $i_0\to k$ and $j\to k$ and composing its $k$-leg with the transition from $j$; two choices agree after taking a common target and equalizing the resulting parallel arrows, by filteredness. The same argument gives compatibility with every arrow of $I$ and uniqueness of the extension. Hence
$$\operatorname{colim}_i H^q(T,(F_i)_{ab})\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ H^q(T,F_{ab}).$$
The explicit leg formula in the cited theorem makes the $i$-leg $H^q(T,(F_i)_{ab}\to F_{ab})$. In particular this holds at $T=tS$, and the maps respect restriction in $S$ because they are induced by the same coefficient maps.

source.place: Tag 09YP (lemma-colimit), constant-site specialization; Tag 0739 (lemma-colim-works-over-collection) is the equivalent fixed-site route

proof.text:
Identify the internal higher invariants, retaining sheafification. Choose an equivariant injective resolution $M\to Q^\bullet$ [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. The exact equivalence $\Phi$ of [lem-sfb-profinite-action-coherent-presentation] sends it to an injective module-sheaf resolution, since the lifting property for monomorphisms transports under the equivalence. Its value on $tS$ is $\Gamma_{R,J}(Q^\bullet)(S)$. Module injectives on this ringed site are acyclic for abelian evaluation at every object [lem-sc-injective-module-abelian-acyclic-zariski]. Abelian sheaves on this small site have enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]. The acyclic-resolution criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity] and its coefficient naturality [lem-sc-acyclic-comparison-natural] therefore identify
$$H^q(\Gamma_{R,J}(Q^\bullet)(S))=H^q(tS,\Phi(M)_{ab}).$$
These are presheaf identifications: compare the underlying abelian resolution with a single abelian injective resolution by a map of sheaf complexes. Evaluation of that same map at each $tS$ commutes with every restriction; its cohomology gives the displayed comparison. Naturality in $M$ follows from the cited comparison theorem. By exact abelian sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], the cohomology sheaf of $\Gamma_{R,J}(Q^\bullet)$ is the sheafification of $S\mapsto H^q(tS,\Phi(M)_{ab})$. This sheafification is therefore the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(M)$, naturally in $M$. This formula does not assert exactness of evaluation on every profinite $S$.

source.place: Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), proof by a single injective resolution; Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), acyclic underlying abelian resolutions

proof.text:
Put $P_i(S)=H^q(tS,(F_i)_{ab})$ and $P(S)=H^q(tS,F_{ab})$. Step 3 says the presheaf map $\operatorname{colim}_i P_i\to P$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], sheafification commutes with colimits. Applying it and step 4 gives an isomorphism on underlying abelian sheaves
$$\operatorname{colim}_i R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N_i)\ \longrightarrow\ R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N).$$
The underlying abelian sheaf of the module colimit is the abelian sheaf colimit [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Each leg is $R^q\Gamma_{R,J}(N_i\to N)$: in step 3 it is induced by that coefficient coprojection, and the step-4 comparison is natural in this map. Thus this is the canonical map in the statement. It is $R$-linear because the derived functor takes values in internal $R$-modules [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. Its inverse is linear: $f^{-1}(ry)=rf^{-1}(y)$ follows by applying the injective linear map $f$. Hence it is an internal-module isomorphism. No uniform bound in $q$ was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NM-080045c93 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node lem-sfb-profinite-action-coherent-presentation and every cited statement in full. This is a first split: in live and side-live the item is unsplit, with no repair note and not dropped. The statement and stmt_deps are unchanged against side-live. Steps 1-5 are correct. Step 1 builds the colimit sectionwise with its induced action. Step 2 moves it through the equivalence Φ. Step 3 applies lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-colimit-of-sites to the constant system of sites P_J over I^op, with the cofinality argument for (i0↓I) written out. Step 4 computes derived invariants as the sheafified presheaf cohomology at tS (Stacks 072W), using injective-module abelian acyclicity, the Leray item 2 criterion and the naturality node. Step 5 assembles the result with exact sheafification (Stacks 0H7B), and its legs are the original coprojections. Edge cases checked: q=0, trivial J, finite J, singleton I, zero modules and S=∅. The new node is true: every profinite J-space T is covered by the free cover J×T→T, Φ(N)(tS)=Γ(N)(S) and Φ(N)(J×S)=N(S); compare Bhatt-Scholze arXiv:1309.1198 Def 4.3.1, Lem 4.3.2 and proof of 4.3.6, which I suggest recording for the WANTED reference. It is not a duplicate: internal-action-site-presentation has only free objects and no tS, and field-profinite-galois-site needs a field. It is strictly smaller than the item. Size: the equivalence needs J×S in the skeleton; under def-weil-size-convention J lies in U, as in the sibling nodes, so I accept it. Batch-5: def-trf-coherent-topos is a general definition of coherent objects whose closure is definitions only. It is not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality statement or proof, so I accept it. I accept all 7 declared tool uses, all generic site and homological lemmas. There is no SGA citation.
